title: Moussaka
imagePrompt: A deep golden-brown crust blankets the top, mottled with darker caramelized patches where the béchamel has bubbled and set in the oven. A cut slice reveals distinct layers: pale golden potato rounds, soft green zucchini, and deep purple-skinned eggplant, all bound by a rich, dark red-brown meat sauce studded with flecks of tomato and onion. The béchamel itself is thick, ivory-colored, and custard-set, holding a clean edge where the slice has been cut, with a faint wisp of steam rising from the warm interior.
subtitle: Layered eggplant, zucchini, and potato with a spiced veal ragù, crowned with a golden baked béchamel. Aria's family recipe.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: Three components: the vegetable layers, the spiced meat sauce, and the milk (béchamel) topping.
items: 5 eggplants, sliced ~1cm thick
4 zucchini (or 1 yellow squash), sliced ~1cm thick
4–5 large potatoes, sliced ~1cm thick
800g minced veal
4–5 tbsp olive oil
1 large onion, finely chopped
2 garlic cloves, finely chopped
1 tbsp tomato paste
1 can chopped tomatoes
1 cinnamon stick
1/3 cup red wine or brandy
1 tsp sugar
Salt & pepper, to taste
1.5 litres full-fat milk
5 tbsp butter
5 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 eggs
Grated Parmesan cheese, to taste (for the béchamel, plus extra for sprinkling between layers)
Nutmeg, to taste
Salt & pepper, to taste
ingredients.callout: Key rule: Roast the eggplant and zucchini until truly soft and fry the potatoes until golden before layering — undercooked veggies leave the finished moussaka watery.

body.html: A classic layered Greek bake: roasted potato, zucchini, and eggplant stacked under a cinnamon-spiced veal ragù, then finished with a thick, glossy béchamel that bakes into a golden crust.

items: Prep the vegetable layers — roast the eggplant and zucchini, fry the potatoes
Build the meat sauce — onion, garlic, veal, wine, tomatoes, and cinnamon
Make the béchamel — butter, flour, milk, then eggs and Parmesan off the heat
Layer — potato, zucchini, eggplant, meat sauce, béchamel
Bake at 200°C until the top is golden brown

body.html: From Aria: Salt each vegetable layer as you go, and sprinkle a little grated cheese over each one for extra flavor.

items: Wash and cut the eggplant, zucchini, and potatoes into slices about 1cm thick.
Lay the eggplant and zucchini slices on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Roast in a hot oven until the slices soften.
Meanwhile, fry the potato slices in olive oil until slightly golden.
Drain the fried potatoes on kitchen paper or a strainer to remove excess oil.

body.html: Don't rush this step: Soft eggplant and zucchini, and well-drained potatoes, keep the layers from turning watery once baked.

slides.title: Build the Meat Sauce
slides.checkboxLabel: Onion, garlic, veal, wine, tomatoes, cinnamon

items: Heat the olive oil in a pot and add the chopped onion and garlic. Simmer until transparent.
Add the minced veal, stirring until it changes color and loses most of its liquid.
Pour in the wine or brandy and stir.
Add the tomato paste, chopped tomatoes, cinnamon stick, sugar, and salt & pepper.
Lower the heat and cook until the meat is softened and the sauce has thickened slightly.

body.html: The cinnamon stick is doing real work here — it's the backbone of the moussaka flavor. Fish it out before layering.

slides.title: Make the Béchamel (Milk Sauce)
slides.checkboxLabel: Butter + flour roux, whisk in milk, finish with eggs

items: Melt the butter in a large pot over low heat.
Add the flour and stir until fully combined with the melted butter.
Start adding the milk little by little, whisking constantly — add more if flour knobs appear.
Keep stirring so the sauce doesn't stick to the bottom of the pot.
Once it starts to thicken and you've used most or all of the milk, switch off the heat.
Stir in the 2 eggs, Parmesan, nutmeg, and salt & pepper until well combined.

body.html: Add the eggs off the heat, not on it. Stirring them into a still-hot (not boiling) sauce keeps them from scrambling.

slides.title: Layer the Moussaka
slides.checkboxLabel: Potato, zucchini, eggplant, meat sauce, béchamel

items: In a large, deep baking pan, add the fried potato slices as the first layer.
Layer the zucchini next, then the eggplant on top.
Sprinkle a little salt and a little grated cheese over each vegetable layer as you go.
Spread the meat sauce evenly over the vegetable layers (remove the cinnamon stick first).
Finish with the béchamel as the top layer, spreading it out to fully cover the pan.

body.html: Order matters: Potato → zucchini → eggplant → meat sauce → béchamel on top.

slides.title: Bake
slides.checkboxLabel: Bake at 200°C until the top browns, ~40 min

items: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Place the pan in the oven.
Bake until the béchamel topping starts to brown, usually around 40 minutes.
Switch off the oven once it's golden and let the moussaka rest a few minutes before slicing.

body.html: Let it rest. Moussaka is much easier to cut into clean slices once it's had a few minutes to set out of the oven.
